Let $s$ be the side length of the square. Then the dimensions of each rectangle are
$s\times\frac{s}{5}$. The perimeter of one of the rectangles is
$s+\frac{s}{5}+s+\frac{s}{5}=\frac{12}{5}s$. Setting $\frac{12}{5}s=36$ inches, we find
$s=15$ inches. The perimeter of the square is $4 s=4(15\text{ in.})=\boxed{60}$ inches.
